chunks: This is a wonderful metaphor, it is as though [the narrator] has likened the rear part of the body with a bag and the eye with a strap. When the strap is let loose the bag cannot retain anything. According to the well-known and reputed view it is the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), but some people have stated it to be of Amīr al-mu’minīn (peace be upon him). al-Mubarrad has mentioned it in his book al-Muqtaḍab under the chapter ‘Words of single letters’. We too have discussed this metaphor in our book named Majāzāt al-āthār an-nabawiyyah.

key_terms.السَّه: the rear part of the body

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the metaphor comparing the eye to a strap and the rear to a container in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Raḍī elucidates the linguistic ingenuity of this metaphor by analyzing the structural relationship between the 'container' (the rear) and the 'strap' (the eye), noting that the latter's release fails to secure the former. This commentary highlights the interplay between grammatical precision and poetic imagery, a hallmark of classical Arabic rhetoric that al-Raḍī further explores in his treatise *Majāzāt al-Athār*. The attribution to both the Prophet and Imam Ali underscores the saying's significance in understanding the linguistic depth of the Ahl al-Bayt's speech.
